quantity.locator: MPIK Heidelberg GALLEX/GNO history page, section "The GALLEX detector and 71Ge extraction procedure"; GNO final paper, Sec. 1
quantity.note: The GNO final paper states 30.3 tons of gallium in a 100-ton gallium chloride target; the MPIK page gives a total solution weight of 101 t.

name: GALLEX
notes: GALLEX (1991-1997) and its successor GNO (1998-2003) are recorded as ONE experiment, with GNO as an alias; there is no separate GNO record.

No dedicated official GALLEX/GNO website was found; the description rests on the MPIK Heidelberg GALLEX/GNO history page (MPIK led GALLEX), the GNO collaboration's final paper and the INSPIRE experiment record.

physics_goals.locator: MPIK Heidelberg GALLEX/GNO history page, sections "GALLEX: a radiochemical GALLium EXperiment to detect solar pp neutrinos" and "GNO: the Gallium Neutrino Observatory"
physics_goals.note: The first sentence of the quote gives the aim of the Ga-71 reaction used by GALLEX and the second the stated aim of its successor GNO, so the goal is read across the two phases of the one experiment.
physics_goals.quote: The threshold of this reaction is 233 keV, low enough to detect neutrinos from the initial proton fusion chain. ... GNO aimed to measure the flux of solar electron neutrinos from the proton-proton fusion during a full solar cycle.
physics_goals.value: Detect low-energy solar neutrinos from the proton-proton fusion chain via the radiochemical gallium-to-germanium reaction and measure their flux

summary.plain: An experiment in an Italian mountain lab that used 30 tonnes of gallium, dissolved in an acid solution, to catch the Sun's lowest-energy neutrinos, the ones from its very first fusion step.
summary.technical: Radiochemical gallium solar-neutrino experiment at LNGS: 30.3 t gallium (as a 101 t GaCl3-HCl solution), sensitive to pp-chain neutrinos via the 71Ga→71Ge reaction (233 keV threshold). Ran as GALLEX 1991-1997 (re-evaluated capture rate 73.1 SNU) then as GNO 1998-2003 (62.9 SNU). GALLEX was run by an international collaboration of French, German, Italian, Israeli, Polish and American scientists headed by the Max-Planck-Institut für Kernphysik, Heidelberg; GNO was headed by the Milano group of INFN.

unique_capabilities.locator: MPIK Heidelberg GALLEX/GNO history page, sections "The GALLEX / GNO Experiments" and "GALLEX: a radiochemical GALLium EXperiment to detect solar pp neutrinos"
unique_capabilities.note: The page gives the 233 keV threshold of the gallium reaction and says the chlorine experiment of Davis was only sensitive above about 0.8 MeV. The radiochemical gallium technique has no technology class of its own in the Atlas; it is described in detector:gallex-gno.technology.
unique_capabilities.quote: The experiment of Davis had to face fundamental problems: It was only sensitive to neutrinos with a energy higher than ∼0.8 MeV ... The threshold of this reaction is 233 keV, low enough to detect neutrinos from the initial proton fusion chain.
unique_capabilities.value: Radiochemical gallium target with a 233 keV threshold, low enough to detect the lowest-energy (pp) solar neutrinos, below the roughly 0.8 MeV sensitivity of the chlorine experiment
